meta.scene_summary: We are building a future of satellites and AI while the foundation is held together by firmware bugs and old receipts.

cooking.headline: Amazon is buying a satellite company because shipping packages to your door wasn't enough.
cooking.summary: Amazon just dropped $11.5 billion on Globalstar to make sure their satellites can talk to your phone from literally anywhere. It is the ultimate flex to ensure your next impulse purchase can be tracked even when you are hiding in the woods.
cooking.plain_english: Amazon has received regulatory approval to acquire the satellite communications company Globalstar for $11.5 billion to support its satellite internet project.

cooking.headline: Hex raises another $100M to make your data notebooks look expensive
cooking.summary: Hex just secured a massive bag to keep building tools that turn your messy SQL queries into shiny interactive dashboards. It's the ultimate way to tell your stakeholders that your data project is definitely 'production-ready' because it has a toggle switch.
cooking.plain_english: The data analysis platform Hex has raised 100 million dollars in new funding to continue developing its software for collaborative data science.

cooking.headline: Valve is trying to keep Steam from becoming a digital landfill for AI-generated shovelware.
cooking.summary: Valve is finally stepping in to address the flood of AI-generated clones and low-effort slop clogging up the store. It's like the teacher finally deciding to ban AI essays after realizing the entire class just turned in the exact same hallucinated report.
cooking.plain_english: Valve is implementing new policies to manage the influx of AI-generated software and games on the Steam platform.

cooking.headline: Nvidia just dropped a transcription model that actually speaks 40 languages
cooking.summary: Nvidia is releasing an open-source transcription model to handle 40 languages, finally giving developers a way to build apps without paying a premium to a black-box API. It's the digital equivalent of finally getting a translator who doesn't charge by the breath.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia has released a free, open-source software tool that can accurately convert spoken audio into text across 40 different languages.

cooking.headline: Tailscale fixed their SSH bug, and somehow the internet didn't implode
cooking.summary: Tailscale managed to patch their SSH investigation without turning the whole network into a house of cards. It's the rare security update that actually leaves you feeling safer instead of just wondering what else they broke.
cooking.plain_english: Tailscale has finished investigating and patching a security vulnerability found in their SSH service.

cooked.headline: A vulnerability in the firmware that runs before your OS just gave hackers the keys to the kingdom.
cooked.summary: We spend all our time securing applications and kernels, only to realize the foundation is basically a screen door in a hurricane. It turns out the most dangerous part of your server is the part that technically doesn't even exist yet.
cooked.plain_english: A security flaw in the system firmware used by most servers allows unauthorized users to execute malicious code before the operating system even starts.

cooked.headline: Harvey raises $500M while a dev drops the open-source version for free
cooked.summary: Harvey landed a half-billion dollar valuation for legal AI, so a developer casually open-sourced a functional alternative to remind everyone that LLMs are just glorified autocomplete. It's the professional equivalent of someone finishing the group project ten minutes after you spent your entire life savings on a fancy binder.
cooked.plain_english: A developer released free, open-source software that performs similar legal document analysis tasks as Harvey, which recently raised 500 million dollars.

cooked.headline: Tech giants suddenly remember intellectual property exists now that AI is scraping their own homework.
cooked.summary: Microsoft and Epic Games are finally calling out AI training as theft, which is a wild pivot for companies that spent years feeding the internet into their own models. It turns out copyright law is only a 'fundamental right' when it's your own proprietary data getting vacuumed up.
cooked.plain_english: Microsoft and Epic Games are now arguing against AI training on copyrighted material, despite previously supporting the technology.

cooked.headline: Qwen has a 'split personality' hidden behind a single neuron
cooked.summary: Researchers discovered that toggling one specific neuron in the Qwen model completely changes its behavior, which is basically the AI version of finding a hidden 'chaos' switch in your codebase. It turns out even the smartest LLMs are just one bit-flip away from a total mid-life crisis.
cooked.plain_english: Scientists found that changing the state of a single specific neuron in the Qwen artificial intelligence model can fundamentally alter how the system behaves and responds.

cooked.headline: Apple's git is still holding onto certificates like a hoarder with old receipts
cooked.summary: Apple's git implementation is still trusting compromised eMudhra certificates that were flagged years ago. It's like keeping the front door unlocked because you lost the key to the deadbolt, but you're sure nobody noticed.
cooked.plain_english: Apple's software for managing code versions still accepts security certificates that were previously identified as compromised.
